How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was hard to figure out when and what was needed to do something. The ACTION NEEDED mark helped!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: MyAriel

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Info-meeting, but it was too late for help with the "accepting the spot" and "deciding to go" part but too early for help with the tecnical stuff with MyAriel and Learning Agreement and fund application. And also it was frusturating that the program was not planned.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Perfect

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose the sustaineble forest topic. It was fantastic and with eskursion.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The content of the course was so good! But the teaching method with a lot of listening was way to one-wayed and hard. Especially without more small breaks.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Perfect

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We have shorter intevals of teaching and way more breaks. We have breaks of 15 minutes every 45 minutes of listening which helps the message to go through better without being distracted by too many other thoughts.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sustainable forest as the only one

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sustainable forest

questions.answer: Easy

questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are very less strict with time and if you agree to meet or leave at 9.00, it will always be at least 15 minutes later.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aperol spritz and mountains

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to the waterfall and ask for breaks during the teaching

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The people at the hostel are very nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Lorenzo was a fantastic teacher and very good at sensing what level his students are on and also answering questions in a elaborating but not too elaborating way.

Also the "get to know each other activity" with Mariola in the first day was very fun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Too few breaks and too much listening. The only breaks were lunch and that's not much of a break when you are socializing and one day also washing dishes (which was very fine to do though).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It would be nice to be more outside during the earlier hours of the day as well and I would have loved for all of us to try the Savannah Life game.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
